From 6231c9e1a9f35b535c66709aa8a6eda40dbc4132 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Prasad Pandit <pjp@fedoraproject.org>
Date: Wed, 3 Jan 2024 13:23:43 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] KVM: x86: make KVM_REQ_NMI request iff NMI pending for vcpu

kvm_vcpu_ioctl_x86_set_vcpu_events() routine makes 'KVM_REQ_NMI'
request for a vcpu even when its 'events->nmi.pending' is zero.
Ex:
    qemu_thread_start
     kvm_vcpu_thread_fn
      qemu_wait_io_event
       qemu_wait_io_event_common
        process_queued_cpu_work
         do_kvm_cpu_synchronize_post_init/_reset
          kvm_arch_put_registers
           kvm_put_vcpu_events (cpu, level=[2|3])

This leads vCPU threads in QEMU to constantly acquire & release the
global mutex lock, delaying the guest boot due to lock contention.
Add check to make KVM_REQ_NMI request only if vcpu has NMI pending.

Fixes: bdedff263132 ("KVM: x86: Route pending NMIs from userspace through process_nmi()")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Prasad Pandit <pjp@fedoraproject.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240103075343.549293-1-ppandit@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>

diff --git a/arch/x86/kvm/x86.c b/arch/x86/kvm/x86.c
index 363b1c080205..25bc52cdf8f4 100644
--- a/arch/x86/kvm/x86.c
+++ b/arch/x86/kvm/x86.c
@@ -5454,7 +5454,8 @@ static int kvm_vcpu_ioctl_x86_set_vcpu_events(struct kvm_vcpu *vcpu,
 	if (events->flags & KVM_VCPUEVENT_VALID_NMI_PENDING) {
 		vcpu->arch.nmi_pending = 0;
 		atomic_set(&vcpu->arch.nmi_queued, events->nmi.pending);
-		kvm_make_request(KVM_REQ_NMI, vcpu);
+		if (events->nmi.pending)
+			kvm_make_request(KVM_REQ_NMI, vcpu);
 	}
 	static_call(kvm_x86_set_nmi_mask)(vcpu, events->nmi.masked);
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `arch/x86/kvm/x86.c`**
- The function `kvm_vcpu_ioctl_x86_set_vcpu_events` was modified to include a conditional check before making the `KVM_REQ_NMI` request. 
- The line `kvm_make_request(KVM_REQ_NMI, vcpu);` was changed to:
  ```c
  if (events->nmi.pending)
      kvm_make_request(KVM_REQ_NMI, vcpu);
  ```
- This change ensures that the `KVM_REQ_NMI` request is only made if `events->nmi.pending` is non-zero, preventing unnecessary requests when there are no NMIs pending.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The modification in `arch/x86/kvm/x86.c` directly addresses a bug where the `KVM_REQ_NMI` request was being made even when there were no NMIs pending for the vCPU. This unnecessary request was causing performance issues due to excessive locking in QEMU, leading to delays in guest boot times. By adding the conditional check, the patch improves the efficiency of the vCPU event handling, reducing lock contention and enhancing overall system performance.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
kvm_make_request(KVM_REQ_NMI, vcpu);
```
```c
vcpu->arch.nmi_pending = 0;
```
```c
atomic_set(&vcpu->arch.nmi_queued, events->nmi.pending);
```
Reason:
The `kvm_vcpu_ioctl_x86_set_vcpu_events` function makes a `KVM_REQ_NMI` request unconditionally, regardless of whether `events->nmi.pending` is zero or not. This results in unnecessary requests being sent, causing vCPU threads in QEMU to frequently acquire and release a global mutex lock, leading to lock contention and delays in guest boot times.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (events->nmi.pending)
    kvm_make_request(KVM_REQ_NMI, vcpu);
```
Reason:
The patch adds a conditional check to ensure that the `KVM_REQ_NMI` request is only made if `events->nmi.pending` is true. This prevents unnecessary requests from being sent when there are no NMIs pending, thereby reducing lock contention and improving guest boot times.
